label: patch_grid_size_floor
shared_hypothesis: The tokenization/patch grid sets a hard minimum-size floor for segmentable structures that data scale and weight adaptation cannot move; only input rescaling or patch-size changes shift it.

members.one_line: SAM has a measurable minimum segmentable object size (~1.5 patches) that is an architectural constant: adaptation cannot fix it, and knowing the constant redirects effort to input scaling
members.note: architectural constant, phase-transition claim

members.one_line: Small-lesion recall versus size follows a sigmoid whose midpoint is set by the tokenization grid, not by data volume, so scaling data cannot move it but changing patch size can.
members.note: same hypothesis as w14A-021: sigmoid midpoint tracks token size; adds medical law + patch-size intervention

members.one_line: Sub-patch wisps are invisible to 16-pixel-patch ViTs: thin-smoke performance scales with patch size while thick-smoke performance does not.
members.note: fold into w14A-021/w14_p1b_061 as amorphous thin-wisp arm; identical tokenization-bottleneck claim

members.one_line: Pretraining-scale gains vanish below a structure-size threshold: scaling curves for medical transfer flatten to zero slope for structures smaller than the effective receptive resolution.
members.note: scaling-curve flattening below size threshold; scaling-law variant

label: prompt_perturbation_instability_signal
shared_hypothesis: Output variance under small prompt perturbations is an informative label-free signal of image-intrinsic ambiguity, domain gap, and failure risk.

members.one_line: Prompt-perturbation instability is a label-free probe that localizes clinically ambiguous boundary regions.
members.note: flip-rate predicts inter-rater disagreement zones

members.one_line: Prompt-jitter robustness radius is a better unsupervised domain-gap meter than IoU-head confidence, telling you where PEFT is needed without labels
members.note: same measurement used as unsupervised domain-gap meter for PEFT triage

members.one_line: SAM point-prompt outputs on smoke are unstable under tiny click jitter, unlike solid objects.
members.note: same measurement as phenomenon characterization on smoke vs solids

members.one_line: Prompt-jitter disagreement maps reproduce human annotator-disagreement maps on smoke, giving a free ambiguity oracle.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_005: identical instability-matches-human-disagreement hypothesis, smoke arm

members.one_line: The minimal click displacement that flips a SAM smoke mask from good to catastrophic is a per-image fragility score that predicts wild failures better than confidence.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-001/w14A-010: minimal-flip-displacement fragility score is the same signal repackaged

members.one_line: Prompt-space adversarial robustness: tiny image perturbations relocate SAM's optimal click position arbitrarily — a new robustness axis that classifier-derived metrics cannot see
members.note: adversarial worst-case click relocation; distinct threat model

label: confidence_inversion_at_ambiguity
shared_hypothesis: Dense/promptable models are most confident exactly where ambiguity or error is highest; miscalibration is a structured inversion (bias), not noise.

members.one_line: Foundation-model confidence peaks on smooth intensity ramps, exactly where clinical boundary uncertainty is greatest, an inversion with measurable structure.
members.note: confidence peaks on smooth ramps where clinical uncertainty is greatest

members.one_line: Where human raters disagree most, single-mask foundation models are most confidently wrong rather than uncertain.
members.note: confidently wrong at high rater-disagreement sites; near w14_p1b_073 as well

members.one_line: Smoke models show confidence inversion: more confident in the ambiguous fringe than at the defensible dense-core boundary.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_008: identical fringe-confidence inversion, smoke arm

members.one_line: Deep ensembles are confidently and unanimously wrong on smoke: epistemic uncertainty is low where error is highest, proving the failure is bias, not variance.
members.note: ensembles unanimously wrong => failure is bias not variance; distinct decomposition claim

members.one_line: Under site shift, dense-prediction confidence stays flat while error rises, and the miscalibration is worse than in classification because spatial correlations hide the drift.
members.note: confidence flat while error rises under site shift; shift-axis variant

label: model_vs_rater_uncertainty_link
shared_hypothesis: Whether model-derived uncertainty reproduces human inter-rater ambiguity, and whether ambiguity-aware supervision improves the main task; contains an explicit tension with XD-02 positive claims.

members.one_line: Voxelwise model uncertainty and inter-rater uncertainty are weakly correlated once distance-to-boundary is controlled, refuting the common claim that model uncertainty captures ambiguity.
members.note: negative claim with distance-to-boundary control

members.one_line: Ensemble disagreement in medical dense prediction concentrates where aleatoric ambiguity lives, so the standard epistemic-aleatoric decomposition mislabels uncertainty sources.
members.note: epistemic/aleatoric decomposition mislabels sources

members.one_line: Training smoke models to also predict the annotator-disagreement map improves the main mask, not just the uncertainty output.
members.note: auxiliary disagreement-prediction head improves main mask

members.one_line: Weighting training loss by rater-disagreement maps changes where models place boundaries but not aggregate Dice, exposing metric blindness to ambiguity handling.
members.note: disagreement-weighted loss moves boundaries, not Dice

members.one_line: Diffusion-based mask samplers reproduce the modes of inter-rater contour distributions but with systematically wrong mode weights, making them qualitatively right and quantitatively unusable.
members.note: diffusion samplers: right modes, wrong weights

label: cheap_output_ensembles
shared_hypothesis: Aggregating cheap output variants (prompts, planes, mask hypotheses, frames) yields calibrated uncertainty or better masks essentially for free.

members.one_line: Uncertainty of promptable models is prompt-conditional, and marginalizing over plausible prompts yields better-calibrated uncertainty than any single-prompt estimate, at quantifiable compute cost.
members.note: prompt-marginal uncertainty better calibrated than single-prompt

members.one_line: Pixelwise disagreement across SAM's three mask hypotheses approximates epistemic uncertainty at zero cost — validate it against deep ensembles once, use it everywhere
members.note: multimask-hypothesis disagreement approximates epistemic uncertainty

members.one_line: Disagreement among axial, coronal, and sagittal inferences of the same 2D model is an accurate label-free voxel error estimator with a determinable exchange rate.
members.note: orthogonal-plane disagreement as voxel error estimator

members.one_line: Averaging SAM mask logits over many jittered prompts reconstructs a soft smoke density map for free.
members.note: jitter-averaged logits reconstruct soft density; same marginalization as w14_p1b_077, different output

members.one_line: Averaging SAM masks over five registered consecutive frames improves smoke IoU for free: smoke moves coherently while its errors do not.
members.note: registered frame averaging; temporal axis

label: internal_quality_signal_ood
shared_hypothesis: SAM-family internal quality signals (IoU head, stability score, softmax confidence) miscalibrate under shift in structured, exploitable ways; the mask selector is often the real OOD bottleneck.

members.one_line: Disagreement between SAM's stability score and its IoU head is an OOD detector: two internal quality signals that decorrelate exactly where the model breaks
members.note: stability-vs-IoU-head decorrelation as OOD detector

members.one_line: SAM's predicted-IoU head is anti-informative on smoke: it ranks its own worst mask first.
members.note: anti-informative selector on smoke; oracle-vs-argmax gap

members.one_line: SAM's predicted-minus-actual IoU gap is itself a smoke detector: overconfidence localizes amorphous matter.
members.note: fold into w14A-020/w14p1c-002: predicted-minus-actual IoU gap is the same signal used as detector

members.one_line: SAM's IoU-head miscalibration under domain shift is directional and fixable with a 2-parameter per-domain temperature, giving a free TTA loss
members.note: miscalibration is directional and 2-parameter fixable

members.one_line: SAM's stability score beats its IoU head as a pseudo-label filter for self-training: the untrained signal outperforms the trained one out-of-domain
members.note: stability score as pseudo-label filter beats IoU head

members.one_line: Quality estimation transfers better than segmentation: SAM's IoU head may remain reliable on domains where its masks fail, enabling self-supervised adaptation with the model as its own judge
members.note: TENSION: claims IoU head transfers better than masks, opposite of w14p1c-002

members.one_line: For rejecting bad smoke masks, max-softmax is beaten by a trivial input statistic (local contrast), an indictment of learned confidence on amorphous targets.
members.note: trivial input statistic beats learned confidence; near w14_p1b_076

members.one_line: Catastrophic segmentation failures are better detected by mask-shape anomaly statistics than by model confidence, because confidence fails silently while shape cannot lie.
members.note: mask-shape anomaly beats confidence for catastrophic-failure detection

label: conformal_conditional_coverage
shared_hypothesis: Conformal mask methods achieve marginal but not conditional coverage; guarantees break along predictable axes (structure, patient, density shift).

members.one_line: Conformal mask pairs achieve marginal coverage but fail per-structure and per-patient conditional coverage in predictable directions, quantifying the gap between statistical and clinical validity.
members.note: marginal-vs-conditional coverage gap, predictable directions

members.one_line: Conformal inner and outer masks are the honest output for smoke, but their coverage guarantees break under smoke-density shift in a predictable direction.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_075 as density-shift arm; same coverage-breakage hypothesis

members.one_line: Conformal prompt sets: distribution-free per-mask coverage guarantees for SAM by calibrating over prompt perturbations instead of model internals
members.note: prompt-perturbation-calibrated conformal sets; method variant

label: amg_saliency_blindness
shared_hypothesis: Automatic 'segment everything' proposal generation inherits an object/saliency prior misaligned with domain-critical targets and misses them at predictable rates.

members.one_line: Segment-everything modes miss pathology at rates predicted by a visual-saliency model, showing automatic mask proposal inherits a saliency prior misaligned with clinical importance.
members.note: miss rate predicted by visual-saliency model

members.one_line: SAM's automatic everything-mode is blind to smoke: it proposes masks for everything except the plume.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_044 as smoke arm; identical AMG-blindness hypothesis

members.one_line: A sampling theorem for prompt grids: derive and validate the minimal automatic-mask-generation grid density guaranteeing coverage of all objects above a given scale
members.note: grid-density coverage theorem; formal variant

label: narrow_ft_erodes_generalist
shared_hypothesis: Narrow fine-tuning erases generalist robustness and secondary capabilities (calibration, ambiguity, refinement, unused prompt channels) while in-distribution validation stays clean.

members.one_line: Brief narrow fine-tuning catastrophically erases the robustness benefits of medical foundation models while preserving in-distribution accuracy, making the erosion invisible to standard validation.
members.note: robustness erosion invisible to standard validation

members.one_line: Fine-tuning SAM on smoke catastrophically degrades its solid-object skill, much more than fine-tuning on a new object class does.
members.note: same erosion hypothesis; adds claim amorphous-target FT is disproportionately destructive

members.one_line: Forgetting in adapted SAM is prompt-channel-selective: box-task PEFT degrades point-prompt zero-shot far more than box zero-shot
members.note: forgetting is prompt-channel-selective

members.one_line: Fine-tuned SAM loses 'ambiguity honesty': its three mask hypotheses collapse into near-duplicates, and nobody measures this collapse
members.note: ambiguity-honesty collapse of multimask head

members.one_line: Domain-adapted SAM gets worse at being corrected: first-click accuracy rises but the refinement loop breaks, visible only in click-curve evaluation
members.note: refinement/correction loop breaks first

members.one_line: PEFT silently destroys IoU-head calibration even while improving masks: an unmeasured forgetting mode inside the decoder
members.note: calibration forgetting inside decoder; near w14A-045 which supplies mechanism

members.one_line: Mask loss and IoU-head loss conflict at the gradient level during PEFT; detaching the quality head into a second phase fixes calibration collapse for free
members.note: gradient-level loss conflict mechanism + two-phase fix

label: propagation_error_compounding
shared_hypothesis: Sequential mask propagation (video memory, slice-to-slice) compounds errors multiplicatively; the failure lives in temporal/sequential association, not appearance.

members.one_line: SAM2's memory bank multiplies first-frame errors: quantify the error-compounding rate and show video adaptation should target memory attention, not the image encoder
members.note: SAM2 memory bank error-compounding rate

members.one_line: Cross-slice prompt propagation error compounds multiplicatively with distance, defining a maximum trustworthy propagation range measurable per anatomy.
members.note: same compounding law for cross-slice propagation; adds trustworthy-range measurement

members.one_line: Memory-based video segmenters shrink smoke masks over time: memory anchors to the dense core and refuses the plume's diffuse growth.
members.note: memory anchors to dense core and refuses diffuse growth; mechanism variant

members.one_line: Video foundation models propagating masks through volumes fail exactly where anatomy changes faster than natural-video motion statistics, a quantifiable mismatch.
members.note: failure where anatomy changes faster than natural-video motion statistics

members.one_line: Video domain gap lives in temporal association, not appearance: tuning only SAM2's memory/object-pointer projections beats encoder LoRA for OOD video at a fraction of the parameters
members.note: adaptation placement: tune memory/object-pointer projections only

label: token_reduction_drops_rare
shared_hypothesis: Token pruning/merging efficiency methods preferentially discard rare small/amorphous targets, coupling efficiency gains to worst-case recall loss.

members.one_line: Token pruning and merging strategies in efficient 3D transformers preferentially discard exactly the tokens containing rare small lesions, making efficiency gains and small-lesion recall fundamentally coupled.
members.note: pruning discards rare-lesion tokens

members.one_line: Token-merging accelerators discard smoke first: efficiency methods trade away amorphous-target accuracy at far above their average cost.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_035 as smoke arm; identical hypothesis. Note tension with w14A-073 (pruning as helpful regularizer)

label: signal_chain_floors
shared_hypothesis: Lossy steps in the acquisition/processing chain (bit depth, dose, bitrate, frame rate, compression, weight quantization) delete target signal before or inside the model, setting hard ceilings invisible to aggregate metrics.

members.one_line: Eight-bit conversion in common foundation-model pipelines erases low-contrast lesions from the input, setting a hard recall ceiling invisible in aggregate metrics.
members.note: 8-bit conversion erases low-contrast lesions; hard recall ceiling

members.one_line: Dose reduction degrades foundation-model segmentation before it degrades human-perceptible image quality, inverting the assumed safety margin.
members.note: dose reduction degrades model before human-perceptible quality

members.one_line: Video compression at CCTV bitrates deletes thin smoke from the signal: smoke segmentation collapses below a bitrate threshold where object segmentation barely notices.
members.note: bitrate threshold deletes thin smoke; near w14_p1b_021

members.one_line: Video smoke segmenters fall off a cliff below 10fps, a silent killer since most CCTV records at 1-5fps.
members.note: fps cliff below 10fps; near w14p1c-119, temporal axis

members.one_line: 4-bit quantization of SAM's encoder damages boundary F-score disproportionately versus region IoU: quantization noise is high-frequency and boundaries live there
members.note: 4-bit weight quantization hurts boundaries disproportionately

members.one_line: JPEG blocks resonate with SAM's patch grid: compression artifacts aligned to the 16-pixel lattice cause a performance cliff that half-patch-shift ensembling removes for free
members.note: JPEG-block/patch-grid resonance cliff

label: noise_floor_of_claims
shared_hypothesis: Reported model differences sit below measurement noise floors: annotation jitter, training-seed variance, and test-set statistical power.

members.one_line: On smoke benchmarks, model-to-human IoU often exceeds human-to-human IoU, putting reported rankings below the annotation noise floor.
members.note: model-human IoU exceeds human-human IoU; rankings below annotation noise

members.one_line: A substantial fraction of reported small-structure error is annotation jitter, measurable by multi-rater re-annotation, meaning true model error on small structures is systematically overestimated.
members.note: same annotation-noise-floor claim for small structures via multi-rater re-annotation

members.one_line: Multi-seed variance of SAM PEFT is large enough to invalidate many reported sub-1.5-point improvements: an audit with prescriptive reporting standards
members.note: multi-seed variance invalidates sub-1.5-point claims

members.one_line: Typical medical segmentation test sets are statistically underpowered to detect the between-model differences the field routinely claims, computable by resampling without new data.
members.note: test sets underpowered by resampling analysis

label: task_definition_variance
shared_hypothesis: Annotation/task-definition conventions vary more than models do; convention is memorized rather than parameterized, and benchmark rankings partly measure convention agreement.

members.one_line: Underspecified task definitions (segment the tumor, with or without necrosis?) account for a measurable share of benchmark error, recoverable by instruction-conditioned evaluation.
members.note: underspecified task definitions account for measurable benchmark error

members.one_line: Three annotation instructions (visible smoke, hazard-level smoke, plume envelope) produce GTs that differ more than competing architectures do.
members.note: three annotation instructions produce GTs differing more than architectures

members.one_line: A train-on-A test-on-B matrix will show smoke segmentation is currently several incompatible tasks sharing one name.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-072 as cross-dataset train/test matrix arm; same conventions-exceed-models hypothesis

members.one_line: Public fire datasets disagree about what fire even is: cross-dataset evaluation will expose annotation-convention gaps larger than model gaps.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-072: fire-definition disagreement arm of the same hypothesis

members.one_line: Switching from single-rater to consensus ground truth flips model rankings on medical benchmarks, showing that leaderboard order partly measures agreement with one annotator's style.
members.note: consensus-vs-single-rater GT flips rankings

members.one_line: Models trained under two contouring conventions cannot interpolate to an intermediate instruction, revealing that convention is memorized, not parameterized.
members.note: models cannot interpolate between conventions; memorization mechanism

label: metric_objective_decoupling
shared_hypothesis: Field-standard segmentation metrics decouple from deployment objectives (clinical error, alarm utility, longitudinal use); rankings do not transfer across metric families.

members.one_line: Above a quality threshold, Dice ranking of models is uncorrelated with ranking by margin-critical clinical error, so leaderboard order stops carrying clinical meaning exactly where models now operate.
members.note: Dice ranking uncorrelated with margin-critical clinical error above quality threshold

members.one_line: Pixel IoU and event-level alarm F1 rank smoke models differently, so the field's metric does not measure the product's objective.
members.note: same decoupling for pixel IoU vs event alarm F1 in smoke

members.one_line: IoU and alarm latency are nearly uncorrelated across smoke models: optimizing segmentation quality does not optimize time-to-detection.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-071 as alarm-latency arm; same IoU-vs-alarm-utility hypothesis

members.one_line: For early smoke smaller than 0.5 percent of the frame, centroid localization error predicts alarm utility; IoU is statistically useless at that scale.
members.note: centroid error is the valid metric for sub-0.5%-frame targets

members.one_line: Boundary metrics and volumetric metrics disagree most on precisely the structures where clinical stakes are highest, making metric choice a hidden clinical judgment.
members.note: boundary vs volumetric metrics disagree most where stakes highest

members.one_line: No single medical segmentation checkpoint Pareto-dominates across metric families and anatomy strata; claimed universal superiority dissolves under multi-objective evaluation.
members.note: no Pareto-dominant checkpoint across metric families

members.one_line: Adding a boundary ignore band to smoke evaluation reorders method rankings, showing current comparisons hinge on unknowable pixels.
members.note: boundary ignore band reorders method rankings

members.one_line: Metric-targeted mask post-processing can move benchmark rankings by margins comparable to claimed methodological advances, exposing the gameability of current evaluation.
members.note: metric-targeted post-processing moves rankings; gameability

members.one_line: Segmentation-derived volumetry errors are dominated by systematic model-specific bias rather than variance, so cross-sectional accuracy metrics mispredict longitudinal utility entirely.
members.note: volumetry bias-vs-variance: cross-sectional metrics mispredict longitudinal utility

label: undertuned_baseline_artifacts
shared_hypothesis: Large claimed gaps/gains shrink under cheap baseline hygiene: selector tuning, threshold offsets, preprocessing choices, spatial priors, protocol bugs, or baseline budgets.

members.one_line: 'SAM fails on X' papers under-tune the baseline: oracle selection among SAM's three masks plus threshold calibration closes a large share of claimed domain gaps
members.note: strong zero-shot protocol closes 30-60% of reported domain gaps

members.one_line: Most of the gap between smoke methods is a global density-threshold offset: one calibrated bias parameter per model erases the SOTA ladder.
members.note: one per-model threshold scalar erases the smoke SOTA ladder; same hygiene-artifact hypothesis

members.one_line: Window and level preprocessing choices dominate reported foundation-model medical performance more than model choice, but are rarely controlled.
members.note: window/level preprocessing dominates model choice; near w14_p1b_013 (signal-physics side)

members.one_line: The embarrassing baseline: a static per-deployment spatial logit prior (one bias map) captures most of the 'adaptation' gain in fixed-camera settings — PEFT papers may be re-learning where things are
members.note: static per-deployment spatial-prior baseline explains 'adaptation' gains

members.one_line: The freezing-bug audit: how often do 'frozen backbone' PEFT results actually train unintended parameters (norms, embeddings, eval-mode mistakes), and how much of reported gains do bugs explain?
members.note: freezing-bug audit: unintended trained parameters explain gains

members.one_line: Expert-level performance claims depend on the annotation time budget given to the human baseline: time-controlled comparisons will move or erase claimed model-human parity.
members.note: human-parity claims depend on human time budget

label: split_leakage_contamination
shared_hypothesis: Entity-level duplication/contamination across splits and into pretraining inflates benchmark results in fingerprintable ways.

members.one_line: Cross-dataset patient duplication silently inflates medical generalization claims: deduplication at the patient level measurably shrinks reported cross-dataset transfer performance.
members.note: patient-level duplication inflates cross-dataset transfer claims

members.one_line: Smoke benchmarks are contaminated by event-level leakage: frames of the same fire sit in both train and test, inflating scores.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_100 as event-level (same-fire frames) arm; identical leakage hypothesis

members.one_line: Web-scale pretrained models show membership-inference signals for public medical benchmark images, implying zero-shot medical results are partially contaminated evaluations.
members.note: membership-inference signals for public benchmarks in web-scale pretraining

members.one_line: Public leaderboard iteration produces measurable test-set adaptation in medical segmentation: late submissions outperform early ones on the public split but not on a sequestered refresh.
members.note: leaderboard test-set adaptation over submission history

members.one_line: Contamination inflates lesion segmentation scores more than organ segmentation scores because idiosyncratic lesion masks are memorizable while regular organ shapes are learnable, an asymmetry that fingerprints contamination.
members.note: lesion-vs-organ contamination asymmetry as fingerprint

label: position_orientation_priors
shared_hypothesis: Models exploit absolute position, orientation, and scene-geometry priors as shortcuts; translating, rotating, or flipping content collapses performance.

members.one_line: Foundation models carry a field-of-view position prior: identical anatomy at unusual image positions is segmented worse, quantified by crop-shift invariance testing.
members.note: field-of-view position prior via crop-shift invariance testing

members.one_line: Lesion-centered cropping conventions in benchmark construction teach models a center-prior shortcut that inflates benchmark scores and collapses under whole-image deployment.
members.note: lesion-centered cropping teaches center prior

members.one_line: Surveillance-trained smoke segmenters run on positional priors: rotating the image collapses them far more than it collapses object segmenters.
members.note: rotation collapses surveillance smoke segmenters; positional-prior arm

members.one_line: Wildfire smoke detectors are horizon-geometry cheaters: vertical flipping collapses their smoke-vs-cloud discrimination.
members.note: vertical flip collapses smoke-vs-cloud discrimination; near w14p1c-020, horizon-geometry arm

members.one_line: SAM has an upright-photo orientation prior: 45-degree rotations hurt more than 90-degree ones, and test-time canonicalization beats weight tuning for orientation-free domains (aerial, microscopy)
members.note: upright-photo orientation prior + test-time canonicalization remedy

members.one_line: Burned-in overlays (rulers, annotations, device text) act as spatial anchors for foundation models: moving them moves the masks.
members.note: burned-in overlays act as spatial anchors

label: context_overrides_evidence
shared_hypothesis: Contextual expectation overrides local evidence: models hallucinate expected content and lean on context crutches, demonstrable by context ablation/inpainting.

members.one_line: Foundation models hallucinate surgically removed organs at high rates, and the hallucination is driven by contextual expectation rather than local evidence, demonstrable by context-ablation.
members.note: hallucinated surgically-removed organs; context-ablation protocol

members.one_line: Inpainting away the smoke source (chimney, flames) while keeping the smoke collapses model predictions, exposing source-context crutches.
members.note: inpainting away smoke source collapses predictions; same context-crutch hypothesis

members.one_line: Under metal and beam-hardening artifacts, foundation models hallucinate plausible anatomy instead of expressing uncertainty, and hallucination rate scales with pretraining scale.
members.note: artifact-zone anatomy hallucination scaling with pretraining

members.one_line: Foundation models complete common organ shape families but fail on congenital variants in a characteristic direction: they normalize the variant toward the common shape, erasing clinically critical morphology.
members.note: congenital variants normalized toward common shape

members.one_line: Steam and smoke are visually indistinguishable near their sources in RGB, so any model separating them must be reading context, testable by cropping it away.
members.note: steam-vs-smoke separation is context reading; crop test

members.one_line: Foundation models cannot complete anatomy beyond the imaged field of view, whereas small 3D-native models can, exposing absent volumetric shape priors.
members.note: TENSION: no shape completion beyond field of view, i.e. missing shape prior where XD-19 claims too much prior

label: absence_blindness
shared_hypothesis: Segmenters cannot represent absence: architectures resist empty masks and text-conditioned models are negation-blind.

members.one_line: Text-guided segmentation models are negation-blind: prompts asserting absence still produce positive masks, a binary failure with direct clinical-safety consequences.
members.note: negated prompts still produce positive masks; representational failure

members.one_line: Open-vocab segmenters are negation-blind on ambiguous classes: prompting smoke, not cloud changes masks by almost nothing.
members.note: fold into w14_p1b_122 as open-vocabulary arm; same negation-blindness hypothesis (locus differs: fusion vs text encoder - note in consolidation)

members.one_line: SAM has an architectural prior against empty masks, making it structurally unable to say 'nothing here' — and PEFT with empty-mask supervision degrades it disproportionately
members.note: architectural prior against empty masks; empty-mask supervision degrades PEFT

label: text_embedding_collision
shared_hypothesis: Text-embedding neighborhood structure (fine-grained collisions, register, idiom priors) predicts which text-prompted segmentation confusions occur.

members.one_line: Text encoders collapse fine-grained medical entity distinctions into overlapping embedding neighborhoods, and this collision structure predicts which text-prompted segmentation confusions occur.
members.note: entity-embedding collisions predict segmentation confusions

members.one_line: Open-vocabulary segmenters give wildly different masks for smoke, steam, vapor, and haze on the same image, and the variance is a class-ambiguity fingerprint.
members.note: synonym-prompt mask variance as class-ambiguity fingerprint; same collision-geometry hypothesis

members.one_line: The same clinical target described in jargon versus lay register produces measurably different masks from text-guided models, violating a basic invariance clinical deployment requires.
members.note: jargon-vs-lay register produces different masks

members.one_line: Attribute prompts (semi-transparent gray turbulent region) beat category prompts (smoke) precisely on rare smoke sub-types where category priors are weakest.
members.note: attribute prompts beat category prompts on rare sub-types

members.one_line: Language-supervised encoders inherit idiomatic smoke (cigarettes, chimneys), predicting a measurable performance ladder across smoke sub-types.
members.note: idiomatic 'smoke' priors from language supervision

members.one_line: For nameable pathologies, a single geometric click beats any text prompt in current medical vision-language segmentation, quantifying how weak language grounding is relative to trivial spatial evidence.
members.note: one geometric click beats any text prompt; grounding-weakness quantification

label: latent_unread_signals
shared_hypothesis: Frozen model internals contain unread task-relevant signals (soft alpha/opacity, sub-voxel boundaries, semantics, part hierarchies, atlases) extractable without retraining.

members.one_line: SAM's logits secretly contain alpha mattes: soft transparency information survives binarization training and can be extracted without retraining
members.note: pre-threshold logits approximate alpha mattes

members.one_line: Logit iso-contours of dense predictors carry recoverable sub-voxel boundary information that discrete masks discard.
members.note: logit iso-contours carry sub-voxel boundary information; same latent-continuous-signal hypothesis

members.one_line: Smoke opacity is linearly decodable from frozen VFM patch features even though mask decoders never use it: the information exists but is unread.
members.note: opacity linearly decodable from frozen patch features; same hypothesis at feature level

members.one_line: Class-agnostic SAM leaks semantics: object class is linearly decodable from mask-token outputs, giving zero-cost semantic labels — and fine-tuning erases this hidden capability measurably
members.note: object class decodable from mask tokens; fine-tuning erases it

members.one_line: An implicit deformable atlas is linearly decodable from medical-adapted foundation-model features; failure of this decoding on specific structures predicts exactly where segmentation fails.
members.note: implicit deformable atlas decodable; decoding failure predicts segmentation failure

members.one_line: Everything-mode NMS throws away the part hierarchy: suppressed mask candidates encode a scene's part-whole tree recoverable for free, without re-running anything
members.note: NMS-suppressed AMG candidates encode part-whole tree

label: edge_dependence_of_boundaries
shared_hypothesis: Foundation-model boundary placement requires photometric edges: contours snap to strongest gradients and fail where edges are absent (amorphous) or convention-offset (clinical).

members.one_line: Foundation models place medical boundaries at intensity gradients even when clinical ground truth is defined functionally, producing a measurable systematic offset.
members.note: edge-snapping bias vs convention-defined clinical boundaries

members.one_line: Drawing a fake thin contour around smoke rescues SAM, proving the failure is edge absence rather than semantic ignorance.
members.note: fake drawn contour rescues smoke; same edge-dependence hypothesis from the absence side

members.one_line: SAM's smoke performance versus opacity is a sharp phase transition, not a gradual decline, revealing an internal edge-detectability threshold.
members.note: sharp opacity phase transition = internal edge-detectability threshold

members.one_line: Blurring images barely hurts SAM on smoke but devastates it on objects, proving smoke performance never came from edges.
members.note: blur dissociation: smoke performance never came from edges

label: mask_statistics_prior_amorphous
shared_hypothesis: Object-centric pretraining mask statistics predict and cause amorphous/translucent-target failure; mask-supervised features actively erase such targets.

members.one_line: SA-1B taught SAM a 'closed-region prior': masks with boundary fractal dimension above a threshold are unrepresentable, predicting exactly which amorphous objects fail
members.note: boundary fractal-dimension threshold predicts which amorphous objects fail

members.one_line: Amorphous regions are underrepresented in promptable-segmentation training masks relative to their pixel frequency, and this representation gap predicts per-class zero-shot failure.
members.note: training-mask frequency gap predicts per-class zero-shot failure; same statistics-prior hypothesis

members.one_line: Self-supervised (DINO-style) features segment smoke better zero-shot than segmentation-supervised features, because mask supervision teaches boundaries smoke does not have.
members.note: DINO features beat mask-supervised features on smoke

members.one_line: Object-centric pretraining makes VFM features of hazy background patches look like clean background, actively erasing translucent occluders.
members.note: object-centric features erase translucent occluders

members.one_line: SAM's three granularity outputs collapse to one mask on smoke, showing its ambiguity head encodes part-whole structure, not density structure.
members.note: multimask head encodes part-whole, not density structure

label: prompt_expressivity_boundary
shared_hypothesis: Some region categories (stuff, process-defined, amorphous) lie outside the prompt language's expressible space: no prompt of any type can select them.

members.one_line: SAM has a 'stuff blindness': unbounded regions (road, water, field) fail not from features but because no prompt type can express 'this material everywhere' — a prompt-language insufficiency result
members.note: stuff blindness: no prompt means 'this material everywhere'

members.one_line: Process-defined regions (wetness, rust, burn marks) sit outside SAM's prompt-expressible space: no click can mean 'the affected area' — an empirical expressivity boundary study
members.note: process-defined regions (wetness, rust) outside prompt-expressible space; same expressivity-boundary hypothesis

members.one_line: Grid-clicking every location inside GT smoke reveals large dead zones where no prompt yields an acceptable mask.
members.note: empirical dead zones: grid-clicking smoke finds no acceptable prompt; smoke arm

label: style_not_anatomy
shared_hypothesis: Fine-tuning learns annotation style and templates rather than domain structure; style transfers across data while anatomy does not.

members.one_line: PEFT fits annotation style, not anatomy: adapters transfer across datasets of the same domain far worse than within annotator styles of different domains — a hidden target-leakage in adaptation research
members.note: adapters transfer within annotator styles, not within domains

members.one_line: Fine-tuned foundation models transfer an institution's contouring style to new anatomy more readily than they transfer anatomical accuracy.
members.note: institutional contouring style transfers more readily than anatomical accuracy; same hypothesis

members.one_line: Single-mask decoders collapse multimodal contour distributions to one rater style rather than an average, and which mode wins is dataset-order dependent.
members.note: single-mask decoders collapse to one rater style, order-dependent

members.one_line: Fine-tuned medical models reproduce near-duplicate training contours for anatomically similar patients, revealing template memorization masquerading as segmentation skill.
members.note: template memorization: near-duplicate contours for similar patients

label: physically_grounded_synthesis
shared_hypothesis: Physically grounded composited/simulated supervision beats wild or generative data at equal volume, and augmentation carries hidden semantics (shortcuts, label poison, prioritization).

members.one_line: Chroma-keyed real smoke composited over new backgrounds gives exact alpha supervision that beats hand-annotated wild data of equal size.
members.note: chroma-keyed real-plume composites with exact alpha beat wild annotations

members.one_line: Physically composited real-plume training data beats diffusion-generated smoke imagery at equal volume, because generative smoke inherits artistic priors.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-043 as vs-diffusion-generated comparison arm; same physically-grounded-synthesis hypothesis

members.one_line: Models trained on physics-simulated images generalize across real sites better than single-site-real-trained models, because simulation training cannot learn real-site shortcuts.
members.note: simulation-trained models immune to real-site shortcuts

members.one_line: Blackbody-temperature-swept synthetic flames close the day-night fire generalization gap better than collecting more single-regime real data.
members.note: blackbody-temperature-swept flames close day-night gap

members.one_line: For sim-to-real smoke segmentation, matching the camera's noise and compression pipeline matters more than matching scattering physics fidelity.
members.note: camera noise/compression pipeline matters more than scattering physics

members.one_line: Binary copy-paste smoke augmentation teaches edge shortcuts: models detect the paste boundary, not the smoke, and alpha-aware pasting removes the shortcut.
members.note: binary copy-paste teaches paste-boundary shortcut; alpha-aware pasting fixes

members.one_line: Standard weather augmentation (synthetic fog and haze) is label poison for smoke training: it injects unlabeled positives into the negative class.
members.note: weather augmentation is label poison for smoke

members.one_line: Physics-based augmentation changes which structures fail rather than uniformly improving robustness, so augmentation choice is a hidden clinical prioritization.
members.note: physics augmentation redistributes failures = hidden clinical prioritization

members.one_line: Background diversity beats plume diversity: at fixed budget, few plumes over many backgrounds trains better smoke models than many plumes over few backgrounds.
members.note: background diversity beats plume diversity at fixed budget

label: attention_stats_free_signal
shared_hypothesis: Transformer attention statistics over a region are training-free per-case quality/saliency signals.

members.one_line: The attention mass a transformer allocates to a structure predicts its segmentation quality, giving a training-free per-case small-structure reliability signal.
members.note: attention mass predicts per-structure segmentation quality

members.one_line: ViT attention entropy over smoke regions is anomalously high, making attention-entropy maps a zero-shot smoke saliency signal.
members.note: attention entropy as zero-shot smoke saliency; same attention-statistic hypothesis

label: register_token_effects
shared_hypothesis: Global/register tokens reroute high-norm global information, with opposite effects by target type: cleaning object transfer vs draining amorphous evidence.

members.one_line: High-norm artifact tokens in SAM's encoder corrupt decoder cross-attention out-of-domain; learning a handful of register-like sink tokens as the only tuned parameters cleans transfer
members.note: learned register-like sink tokens clean OOD transfer

members.one_line: Register tokens make smoke localization worse: global tokens absorb haziness as image-level style, draining it from patch features.
members.note: TENSION: registers absorb haziness and hurt smoke localization; same mechanism, opposite sign

label: corruption_transfer_failure
shared_hypothesis: Corruption-robustness rankings and fingerprints do not transfer across domains; domain physics reorders them.

members.one_line: Natural-image corruption robustness does not rank-transfer to medical corruptions: checkpoints ordered by natural robustness reorder under physics-based medical perturbations.
members.note: natural-corruption robustness does not rank-transfer to medical perturbations

members.one_line: The corruption-robustness fingerprint of smoke segmentation is qualitatively unlike object segmentation, and synthetic fog actually raises smoke recall.
members.note: smoke corruption fingerprint qualitatively different; synthetic fog raises smoke recall

label: model_transcending_failures
shared_hypothesis: Failure structure is model-transcending, driven by shared data/prior blind spots: difficulty scores and mined failures transfer across models and generations.

members.one_line: Case difficulty is a stable, model-transcending latent variable: a difficulty score fitted on one model generation predicts failures of future generations, bounding what modeling progress alone can fix.
members.note: difficulty latent fitted on one generation predicts the next

members.one_line: Failure cases mined against SAM transfer to other vision foundation models at high rates, indicating shared pretraining blind spots rather than architecture quirks.
members.note: failures mined against SAM transfer to other VFMs; same shared-blind-spot hypothesis

members.one_line: The spatial autocorrelation structure of segmentation errors differs qualitatively between foundation models and task-specific models, and this signature identifies error provenance without ground truth.
members.note: error spatial-autocorrelation signature identifies provenance

label: scale_prior_mismatch
shared_hypothesis: Apparent domain gaps are substantially scale-prior mismatches, fixable by input rescaling rather than weight adaptation.

members.one_line: SAM features are scale-equivariant only inside a 'sweet band' of object sizes; outside it, input rescaling beats any weight-space adaptation
members.note: scale-equivariance sweet band; rescaling beats adaptation outside it

members.one_line: Pediatric failure of adult-trained foundation models is mostly a scale prior, not an anatomy gap: metric rescaling recovers a large share, and the unrecovered residue localizes to genuinely developmental structures.
members.note: pediatric failure mostly a scale prior; metric rescaling decomposition

members.one_line: Downsampling images improves SAM smoke segmentation by destroying the background detail it wrongly latches onto.
members.note: inverse case: downsampling helps smoke by destroying distractor detail

label: refinement_pathologies
shared_hypothesis: Interactive refinement is not monotone: click order, count, and user style produce path-dependent and sometimes worsening outcomes, with measurable interaction laws.

members.one_line: SAM degrades beyond a critical number of point prompts because SA-1B interactive training rarely exceeded a few clicks per mask
members.note: degradation beyond critical click count from SA-1B statistics

members.one_line: Iterative click refinement is non-monotonic on smoke: added corrective clicks can make SAM masks worse.
members.note: corrective clicks make smoke masks worse; same non-monotonicity hypothesis

members.one_line: Interactive SAM is path-dependent: the same final set of clicks yields different masks depending on click order
members.note: click-order path dependence

members.one_line: Prompt attention collapse: with many prompts, decoder cross-attention mass concentrates on 1-2 prompt tokens, explaining diminishing returns of extra clicks
members.note: prompt attention collapse mechanism

members.one_line: Iterative click refinement converges to the prompting user's personal contouring bias, not toward consensus truth, making interactive accuracy an interaction-style artifact.
members.note: refinement converges to user's personal bias, not consensus

members.one_line: Clicks-to-target-accuracy follows a power law in a structure-complexity statistic, giving each model a measurable interaction exponent that summarizes its medical usability.
members.note: clicks-to-accuracy power law; interaction exponent

members.one_line: Weight-averaging (EMA) during PEFT stabilizes interactive click-curves far more than single-shot mIoU: the cheap trick that specifically fixes the metric nobody measures
members.note: EMA specifically stabilizes click curves

members.one_line: Train the prompt encoder with reinforcement learning on clicks-to-acceptance: optimize the interaction loop directly instead of per-mask loss
members.note: RL directly on the interaction loop

label: click_simulation_validity
shared_hypothesis: Ground-truth-derived click simulation misestimates real interactive performance; real user click distributions change method rankings and expose correlated human-model failure.

members.one_line: Standard center-click simulation overestimates interactive performance because real boundary-focused clicking interacts destructively with prompt encoders, a measurable simulator-validity failure.
members.note: center-click simulation overestimates; simulator-validity failure

members.one_line: Everyone trains PEFT with prompts sampled from ground truth, but humans click where errors are salient: saliency-matched prompt simulation changes which adapter wins
members.note: saliency-matched prompt simulation changes which adapter wins; same simulator-validity hypothesis

members.one_line: Learn the click simulator from real user logs and make it a first-class released artifact: adapters trained under logged-behavior simulation transfer to humans better than any synthetic policy
members.note: learn the click simulator from real logs; release as artifact

members.one_line: Clinicians place prompts precisely where they are uncertain, which is where models are also least reliable, so real interactive performance is bounded by correlated human-model failure.
members.note: clinicians click where uncertain: correlated human-model failure bound

members.one_line: Clicking the rim of a glass yields far better SAM masks than clicking its center, the reverse of opaque objects, motivating class-conditional prompt policies.
members.note: rim-vs-center click policy inverts for glass; class-conditional prompting

members.one_line: SAM point prompts carry a hidden distance-to-boundary prior: mask topology changes systematically with where inside the object you click
members.note: click-position distance-to-boundary prior; mechanism behind placement sensitivity

members.one_line: Oracle-prompt evaluation inflates and reorders PEFT method rankings: the field's league tables may not survive realistic prompting
members.note: oracle-prompt evaluation inflates and reorders PEFT rankings

label: box_prompt_compactness
shared_hypothesis: Box (and point) prompts impose a compact-object prior; quality falls with box occupancy and elongation, failing worst on thin/elongated/amorphous targets.

members.one_line: Box prompts act as hard spatial gates, not soft priors: SAM almost never segments beyond the box even when the object visibly continues
members.note: boxes act as hard spatial gates, not soft priors

members.one_line: Box prompts impose a compact-object prior: segmentation quality degrades predictably as the target's box-occupancy ratio falls, failing worst on thin diagonal structures.
members.note: box-occupancy degradation law, thin diagonal structures worst

members.one_line: Extreme aspect-ratio boxes (>20:1) fall outside SAM's prompt statistics and cause systematic under-segmentation of thin elongated structures
members.note: extreme aspect-ratio boxes under-segment thin structures; near w14_p1b_038

members.one_line: Prompt-placement sensitivity of promptable models grows with structure elongation following a measurable law, making tubular anatomy intrinsically prompt-hostile.
members.note: point-placement sensitivity grows with elongation; near w14_p1b_038, point-prompt arm

members.one_line: Box prompts beat point prompts disproportionately on smoke because extent cannot be inferred from texture.
members.note: boxes beat points on smoke because extent is not inferable from texture

label: negative_click_semantics
shared_hypothesis: Negative prompts are undertrained and interpreted geometrically rather than semantically.

members.one_line: Negative clicks are undertrained relative to positive clicks: an information-matched negative click helps far less than a positive one
members.note: information-matched negative click helps far less than positive

members.one_line: Negative clicks are interpreted geometrically (push boundary away) not semantically (exclude tissue class), so excluding pathology from an organ mask fails in a characteristic way.
members.note: negative clicks push boundaries geometrically instead of excluding tissue class; same deficit, mechanism arm

label: natural_image_statistics_prior
shared_hypothesis: Granularity and shape choices follow natural-image object statistics rather than domain-appropriate statistics.

members.one_line: Given one ambiguous point in nested anatomy, foundation models choose the granularity level whose size matches natural-image object statistics, not the clinically salient level.
members.note: ambiguous-point granularity matches natural-image size statistics, not clinical salience

members.one_line: SAM's three multimask tokens have stable whole/part/subpart roles across domains, enabling granularity routing by tuning only one token embedding
members.note: stable whole/part/subpart token roles enable granularity routing

members.one_line: Predicted contour curvature statistics of foundation models match natural-image object statistics, not anatomical shape statistics.
members.note: predicted contour curvature statistics match natural images, not anatomy

label: distillation_capability_loss
shared_hypothesis: Distillation preferentially loses secondary capabilities (interaction loop, ambiguity band) that headline metrics do not track.

members.one_line: Interactivity is the hard-to-distill component: students distilled from adapted SAM inherit single-shot accuracy but lose the correction loop, and nobody measures it
members.note: students lose the correction loop, keep single-shot accuracy

members.one_line: Distilling a foundation smoke segmenter into an edge model loses the ambiguous transition band first, and soft-alpha distillation targets fix exactly that loss.
members.note: edge distillation loses the ambiguous transition band first; soft-alpha targets fix it

label: ambiguity_aware_supervision
shared_hypothesis: Supervising ambiguous regions with hard binary labels is harmful; ignore-bands, soft/matting targets, ranking protocols, and asymmetric label bias beat hard supervision.

members.one_line: Training with an ignore band over the smoke transition zone beats training on hard labels there, at identical data volume.
members.note: ignore band over transition zone beats hard labels at equal data

members.one_line: Training transparent-object models with rim-band supervision only (ignore the interior) matches full-mask supervision, because interior labels are noise.
members.note: rim-band-only supervision matches full masks (interior labels are noise); near w14p1c-017

members.one_line: Models trained on binary smoke labels are confidently wrong in the transition band; disagreement-weighted label smoothing fixes calibration for free.
members.note: disagreement-weighted label smoothing fixes calibration; near w14p1c-017

members.one_line: Binary masks are a category error for smoke: training as alpha matting and thresholding afterward beats direct binary training even on binary IoU.
members.note: train as alpha matting, threshold after; beats binary even on binary IoU

members.one_line: Humans disagree on binary smoke boundaries but agree on relative opacity ordering, so ranking annotation is the consistent (and cheaper) protocol.
members.note: opacity-ranking annotation protocol: humans agree on ordering, not boundaries

members.one_line: Off-the-shelf hair/fur matting models, given a trimap from a coarse smoke detector, outperform dedicated smoke segmentation architectures.
members.note: off-the-shelf matting models + trimap beat dedicated architectures

members.one_line: Smoke models tolerate dilated ground truth far better than eroded ground truth, so biasing annotation outward is a free training win.
members.note: dilated-vs-eroded GT tolerance asymmetry; bias annotation outward

members.one_line: Training fire models with amodal labels (fire extent including smoke-occluded parts) improves even the visible-flame segmentation.
members.note: amodal fire labels improve visible-flame segmentation

label: opacity_aware_metrics
shared_hypothesis: Opacity/density-aware metrics match human quality judgments where binary IoU and boundary-F fail.

members.one_line: A density-weighted boundary metric agrees with human judgments of smoke mask quality where standard boundary F-measure fails.
members.note: density-weighted boundary metric agrees with human judgment

members.one_line: Soft IoU on predicted opacity correlates with human quality judgments of smoke masks better than binary IoU at any threshold.
members.note: fold into w14p1c-075 as region-level soft-IoU arm; same opacity-aware-metric hypothesis

label: peft_outcome_prediction
shared_hypothesis: PEFT outcomes (gain, ceiling, budget, go/no-go) are predictable from cheap pre-adaptation diagnostics.

members.one_line: A pre-adaptation diagnostic that forecasts PEFT gains: the linear-probe gap on frozen SAM features predicts which tasks PEFT can and cannot fix
members.note: linear-probe gap on frozen features forecasts PEFT gains

members.one_line: Zero-shot IoU linearly predicts the post-PEFT ceiling across domains: a two-variable law that triages adaptation investments
members.note: zero-shot IoU linearly predicts post-PEFT ceiling; same cheap-predictor hypothesis

members.one_line: A sample-efficiency scaling law for SAM PEFT: predict labels-needed-for-target-IoU from prompt informativeness before annotating anything
members.note: labels-needed scaling law from prompt informativeness

members.one_line: Measure the intrinsic dimension of SAM adaptation (random-subspace training) and show it is predictable from unlabeled domain statistics — a predictive theory of PEFT budget
members.note: intrinsic dimension of adaptation predictable from unlabeled statistics

members.one_line: Camouflage as the universal hardness axis: performance on camouflaged-object benchmarks predicts a domain's PEFT ceiling for low-contrast targets — a transferable hardness ruler
members.note: camouflage benchmarks as transferable hardness ruler

members.one_line: The negative-transfer boundary: map the (label-count, domain-gap) plane where PEFT hurts versus helps, producing the field's missing go/no-go chart
members.note: negative-transfer go/no-go boundary map

label: zeroshot_adapted_continuum
shared_hypothesis: A continuum between zero-shot and adapted behavior is traversable post hoc; weight-space and output-space interpolation trade differently.

members.one_line: Adapter scale interpolation at inference (alpha from 0 to 1) traces a smooth in-domain/zero-shot Pareto family from a single trained adapter — one training run, a continuum of models
members.note: adapter scale interpolation traces a Pareto family

members.one_line: Pixelwise logit fusion of zero-shot and adapted SAM, gated by the IoU head: output-space ensembling that beats weight-space interpolation on the robustness-accuracy front
members.note: IoU-gated logit fusion claims to beat weight interpolation; direct competitor experiment

label: prompt_side_adaptation
shared_hypothesis: Much of the domain gap is prompt-interpretation gap, fixable on the prompt side: virtual clicks, prompt-encoder tuning, prompt-subspace and prefix PEFT.

members.one_line: Most of SAM's domain gap may be prompt-interpretation gap: a tiny learned click-remapping MLP (image-conditioned virtual clicks) recovers it without touching the backbone
members.note: image-conditioned virtual-click remapping MLP recovers the gap

members.one_line: Test-time prompt optimization: gradient-descend the prompt embedding (not the weights) against the IoU head to find 'virtual clicks' better than any human click
members.note: test-time prompt-embedding optimization against IoU head; same virtual-click hypothesis, training-free arm

members.one_line: The frozen-prompt-encoder convention is unjustified: click-semantics gaps (what a click means in this domain) are cheaply fixable by prompt-encoder tuning and unfixable by encoder LoRA — test the convention everyone inherits
members.note: frozen-prompt-encoder convention audit; same claim that the prompt side is the fixable locus

members.one_line: Prompt-token activations occupy a tiny linear subspace; tuning only that subspace ('prompt-subspace PEFT') could match LoRA at 1/1000 the parameters
members.note: prompt-token subspace PEFT at 1/1000 parameters

members.one_line: Decoder prefix tokens as task identity: K learned virtual tokens prepended to prompts encode a task in ~8KB, enabling instant task switching and a measurable 'task capacity' of SAM's decoder
members.note: decoder prefix tokens as 8KB task identity

label: hard_negative_value
shared_hypothesis: Hard negatives (model-mined or scene-curated) are the highest-value supervision per label for adaptation and precision.

members.one_line: Mine hard negatives from everything-mode: AMG's false-positive masks on target-domain images are the highest-value supervision for PEFT, worth more per label than random ground-truth masks
members.note: AMG false positives as highest-value PEFT supervision

members.one_line: Adding hard-negative scenes (fog, sunsets, steam) without any new positives improves smoke-detector precision more than doubling the positive set.
members.note: hard-negative scenes without new positives beat doubling positives; same hard-negative-value hypothesis

members.one_line: Fewer than ten embedding clusters cover over 90 percent of a smoke detector's false positives, making targeted negative collection tractable.
members.note: few embedding clusters cover most false positives; makes targeting tractable

label: reflection_confusion
shared_hypothesis: Models bind objects/fire to reflections and specular structure; separating real from reflected requires context or polarization cues.

members.one_line: Masks leak into mirrors: SAM merges objects with their reflections, and a rank-1 surgical decoder edit might suppress reflection-binding as a model-editing case study
members.note: reflection-binding in mirrors; rank-1 decoder edit case study

members.one_line: Fire reflections on windows, water, and metal are the dominant false-positive class of fire segmenters, and they are separable by context, not appearance.
members.note: fire reflections are the dominant false-positive class, separable by context

members.one_line: Mirror-versus-window confusion is auto-diagnosable: check whether the predicted region contains the camera-side scene.
members.note: mirror-vs-window auto-diagnosis via camera-side scene check

members.one_line: Removing specular highlights collapses SAM on glass, showing masks are anchored to reflections rather than to the object.
members.note: glass masks anchored to specular highlights

members.one_line: A single rotatable polarizing filter separates real fire from reflected fire: direct flame emission is unpolarized, reflections are partially polarized.
members.note: polarization separates emission from reflection

label: temporal_motion_cheap_signals
shared_hypothesis: Temporal statistics (variance, flow divergence, spectral signatures) are cheap dominant signals for amorphous targets that beat or boost deep models.

members.one_line: On static cameras, a thresholded per-pixel temporal-variance map beats zero-shot SAM at smoke segmentation, an embarrassing baseline the field skips.
members.note: thresholded temporal-variance map beats zero-shot SAM; embarrassing baseline

members.one_line: Temporal-variance pseudo-labels from static cameras pretrain smoke models that beat human-label-only training with a fraction of the annotation.
members.note: same signal as pseudo-label pretraining; near w14p1c-051

members.one_line: Classical background subtraction plus SAM prompting (change-blob centroid as click) beats both parts alone, even on stabilized moving-camera footage.
members.note: background subtraction + SAM prompting hybrid

members.one_line: Optical-flow divergence separates expanding smoke from moving solid objects, a one-channel cue that cuts moving-object false positives.
members.note: optical-flow divergence separates expanding smoke from solids

members.one_line: Real smoke motion follows turbulent spatiotemporal spectra that flags, water, and foliage do not, enabling a physics-signature classifier of moving regions.
members.note: turbulence spatiotemporal spectra classifier; near w14p1c-054

members.one_line: Video fire models ignore flame flicker entirely: temporal downsampling to 5fps costs them nothing, proving the strongest physical cue goes unused.
members.note: diagnosis: fire models ignore flicker entirely

members.one_line: A two-band temporal filter (high-frequency flicker for fire, low-frequency drift for smoke) improves joint fire-smoke segmentation more than doubling model size.
members.note: two-band temporal filter exploits flicker+drift; near w14p1c-034, fix arm

members.one_line: On static cameras, smoke alpha is recoverable unsupervised by decomposing each frame into a background layer plus a smoke overlay constrained by neighboring frames.
members.note: unsupervised alpha via background+overlay decomposition on static cameras

label: translucent_occluder_erasure
shared_hypothesis: On translucent/amorphous targets the model segments what is behind, not the medium; glass and smoke fail on distinct axes (interior vs boundary).

members.one_line: SAM sees through thin smoke: its dominant error is returning the occluded background object, not a wrong smoke boundary.
members.note: SAM sees through thin smoke and returns the background object

members.one_line: SAM's mask for a glass object is determined more by what is behind the glass than by the glass itself.
members.note: glass mask determined by what is behind the glass; same see-through hypothesis, transparent arm

members.one_line: Transparent and amorphous targets fail on opposite axes: glass fails in the interior, smoke fails at the boundary, and this two-axis taxonomy predicts which fix works.
members.note: two-axis failure taxonomy predicting which fix works

members.one_line: The refraction-induced warp field of the background is the strongest transparent-object cue, and ViTs are nearly blind to it.
members.note: refraction warp field is the strongest cue and ViTs are blind to it

members.one_line: Liquid fill level flips the topology of SAM's glass masks (full = one blob, empty = ring), a controllable axis for systematic failure mining.
members.note: liquid fill level flips mask topology; controllable failure axis

label: color_cue_reliance
shared_hypothesis: Color-channel reliance is task-split: SAM barely uses color, flame segmentation needs chromaticity, smoke does not.

members.one_line: SAM barely uses color: channel-permutation near-invariance would overturn preprocessing lore for grayscale-native domains
members.note: channel-permutation near-invariance of SAM

members.one_line: Grayscale conversion cripples fire segmentation but barely touches smoke, splitting the two tasks by their dominant cue.
members.note: grayscale conversion cripples fire but not smoke; same color-reliance audit split by task

label: conditional_calibration
shared_hypothesis: Calibration is conditional on structure, size, and granularity: global temperature scaling fails, cheap conditional recalibration works.

members.one_line: Temperature scaling fitted on one anatomy does not transfer to any other anatomy, revealing that dense-prediction miscalibration is structure-specific rather than model-global.
members.note: anatomy-fitted temperature does not transfer; miscalibration is structure-specific

members.one_line: Calibration inverts with structure size: models are overconfident on small structures and underconfident on large ones, so size-conditional recalibration beats global temperature scaling.
members.note: calibration inverts with structure size; size-conditional recalibration

members.one_line: Models calibrated at coarse label granularity are systematically miscalibrated at fine granularity, so hierarchy-aware calibration is necessary for subregion-level clinical use.
members.note: coarse-granularity calibration breaks at fine granularity

members.one_line: OOD track loss in SAM2 is largely an occlusion-head calibration failure: one temperature scalar per domain restores tracking without touching segmentation
members.note: SAM2 occlusion-head per-domain temperature restores tracking

label: error_redistribution
shared_hypothesis: At equal aggregate metric, models differ in error taxonomy and per-case redistribution: improvements often fix easy cases while breaking hard ones.

members.one_line: Reported average improvements of foundation models over specialists come from redistributing errors across cases (fixing easy, breaking hard), detectable as increased per-case variance at improved means.
members.note: average gains from redistributing errors; per-case variance rises

members.one_line: At equal Dice, foundation models and specialists make categorically different kinds of errors (semantic confusions versus boundary noise), so error taxonomy, not magnitude, is what changed with the paradigm shift.
members.note: categorically different error taxonomies at equal Dice; near w14_p1b_109

label: processing_fingerprints
shared_hypothesis: Sensor/software processing fingerprints (reconstruction kernels, resampling signatures, rolling shutter) dominate model behavior and act as shortcuts.

members.one_line: Reconstruction-kernel texture is a stronger determinant of foundation-model segmentation quality than the anatomy being segmented, revealed by kernel-swapped paired reconstructions.
members.note: reconstruction-kernel texture outweighs anatomy; kernel-swapped pairs

members.one_line: Resampling-software fingerprints (interpolation signatures) are detectable by foundation models and exploited as dataset shortcuts, inflating within-benchmark generalization claims.
members.note: resampling-software interpolation signatures exploited as shortcuts; same fingerprint hypothesis

members.one_line: Rolling-shutter banding under flame flicker creates a spurious texture that video fire models key on, failing silently on global-shutter cameras.
members.note: rolling-shutter flicker banding as spurious cue; global-shutter failure

label: feature_space_ood_error
shared_hypothesis: Whether feature-space distance to the pretraining manifold predicts task error; direct conflict on familiar-but-hard inputs.

members.one_line: Feature-space distance to the pretraining manifold predicts dense-prediction error better than output-level uncertainty, unifying OOD detection and error estimation for medical foundation models.
members.note: feature distance predicts dense-prediction error, unifying OOD detection and error estimation

members.one_line: Smoke is familiar-but-not-understood: OOD detectors on VFM features call smoke images in-distribution even though task error is OOD-grade.
members.note: TENSION: smoke is feature-space in-distribution while task error is OOD-grade; direct counterexample claim

label: small_structure_training_pathologies
shared_hypothesis: Distinct mechanisms limiting small-structure learning (losses, mining, mixing, curricula); no hypothesis-level duplicates besides the flagged pair.

members.one_line: Oversampling small objects during PEFT backfires beyond a ratio: below the encoder's resolvable size, their gradients are label noise that degrades everything else
members.note: small-object oversampling below resolvable size is label noise; near w14_p1b_065 (loss-side gradient ceiling)

members.one_line: Overlap-based losses impose a mathematical gradient ceiling on small structures, and gradient-contribution accounting predicts which structures cannot improve regardless of training length.
members.note: overlap-loss gradient ceiling on small structures

members.one_line: Reweight training loss by prompt information content instead of resampling by instance size: size-balancing corrects the wrong variable in promptable-model adaptation
members.note: reweight by prompt information content, not instance size

members.one_line: Texture-versus-shape reliance of foundation models inverts with structure scale in medical images: texture drives large-structure success but is unavailable at small scales, explaining the small-structure cliff.
members.note: texture-shape reliance inverts with structure scale

members.one_line: Below a measurable size threshold, detect-then-segment pipelines beat end-to-end dense prediction, and the threshold is predictable from the dense model's recall curve, unifying two architecture camps.
members.note: detect-then-segment beats dense below predictable size threshold

members.one_line: Rare-but-large and common-but-small structures fail through different mechanisms (representation scarcity versus resolution), demonstrable by opposite responses to resampling and data-weighting interventions.
members.note: rare-large vs common-small fail via different mechanisms

members.one_line: Super-resolution preprocessing improves small-structure recall only when the SR model is trained on matched modality physics; mismatched SR increases confident false positives, a net clinical harm.
members.note: modality-matched super-resolution helps; mismatched SR harms

members.one_line: Hard-example mining collapses onto a few structure types and starves the rest, so mining improves targeted structures while measurably degrading unmined small structures, a hidden redistribution.
members.note: hard-example mining redistributes harm to unmined structures

members.one_line: Final-resolution token budget, not curriculum order, determines small-structure performance: coarse-to-fine training schedules are interchangeable at matched final budgets.
members.note: final token budget, not curriculum order, determines outcome

label: topology_structure_priors
shared_hypothesis: Topology and structural-prior failures and fixes; distinct hypotheses per structural property.

members.one_line: SAM's 2-layer decoder is the topology bottleneck: iterating the decoder with tied weights at inference (zero training) improves multi-component and holed masks
members.note: decoder iteration with tied weights fixes topology at inference

members.one_line: Topological errors of foundation models concentrate at low-contrast interfaces in a predictable census, so topology violations are localizable in advance from image statistics alone.
members.note: topological errors localizable in advance from image statistics

members.one_line: Foundation models produce anatomically impossible label adjacencies at rates far exceeding 3D-native models, and the impossible-pair rate is a sensitive capability metric invisible to Dice.
members.note: impossible label adjacencies as Dice-invisible capability metric

members.one_line: Topology-constrained decoding improves average metrics but degrades performance on post-surgical and variant anatomy, quantifying the cost of enforcing priors that reality sometimes violates.
members.note: topology constraints degrade post-surgical/variant anatomy

members.one_line: Subregion masks of hierarchical predictions violate part-whole containment at measurable rates, and enforcing consistency reallocates error in clinically nontrivial ways rather than simply fixing it.
members.note: part-whole containment violations; enforcing reallocates error

members.one_line: Branch-point recall in tubular-tree segmentation declines with branching angle acuity in a model-transcending pattern, indicating a representational limit on acute bifurcations, not a data deficiency.
members.note: branch-point recall vs bifurcation acuity representational limit

members.one_line: Anatomical ordering constraints along body axes are learnable by sequence models over organ tokens but are demonstrably absent from dense decoders, explaining a class of gross mislabelings.
members.note: body-axis ordering constraints absent from dense decoders

members.one_line: IoU hides the worst failure on fences and meshes: models output topologically solid masks for perforated objects, measurable by Euler-number mismatch.
members.note: Euler-number mismatch on perforated objects invisible to IoU

members.one_line: Topology-change frames (plume splitting or merging) account for the majority of video smoke tracking failures, a countable and mineable event class.
members.note: plume topology-change frames dominate video tracking failures

label: sam_architecture_audits
shared_hypothesis: Audits of specific SAM architectural components; distinct mechanisms.

members.one_line: The dense mask-prompt pathway is nearly a no-op for out-of-domain inputs: an ablation audit of SAM's least-understood input channel
members.note: dense mask-prompt pathway near-no-op audit

members.one_line: The 4x upscaling head, not the encoder, creates most boundary error under domain shift — probe the 256x256 logits before blaming features
members.note: 4x upscaling head causes boundary error, not encoder

members.one_line: A constant half-pixel boundary offset from bilinear logit upsampling: every SAM mask is systematically shifted, and a one-parameter correction improves all results universally but invisibly
members.note: constant half-pixel bilinear offset; universal one-parameter fix

members.one_line: Decoder attention heads specialize into boundary heads and region heads: per-head gating (~100 parameters) as an interpretable, ultra-cheap adaptation mechanism
members.note: boundary-vs-region decoder head specialization; per-head gating

label: positional_resolution_engineering
shared_hypothesis: Positional-encoding and resolution handling effects; distinct mechanisms.

members.one_line: Fourier positional encoding of prompts creates sub-pixel grid aliasing: click effectiveness oscillates periodically with position at the patch frequency
members.note: sub-pixel Fourier-PE aliasing of click effectiveness

members.one_line: Mask errors cluster at window-attention seams out-of-domain: SAM's windowed ViT blocks leave a spatial fingerprint that adaptation should target, not blur over
members.note: window-attention seam error fingerprint

members.one_line: Tiling-vs-resizing for high-resolution images interacts with prompt type: point prompts suffer from tiling, box prompts from resizing — an unmeasured 2x2 interaction
members.note: tiling-vs-resizing by prompt type 2x2 interaction

members.one_line: Positional-embedding-only tuning after interpolation recovers most of the high-resolution adaptation gain at ~0.01% of parameters
members.note: positional-embedding-only tuning after interpolation

members.one_line: Square padding biases masks near the padded side: SAM outputs have a measurable error gradient toward padding, fixable with a learned pad token
members.note: padding-side error gradient; learned pad token

members.one_line: Silent bug with a signature: at non-native resolutions, image-side and prompt-side positional encodings must be rescaled jointly, and implementations that rescale only one produce a diagnosable constant click-offset
members.note: joint image/prompt PE rescaling bug with diagnosable signature

label: peft_placement_map
