shared_hypothesis: Where to place adaptation parameters in SAM; distinct placement hypotheses.

members.one_line: Tune only the hypernetwork MLP that turns mask tokens into dynamic filters: possibly the highest-leverage 3-layer module in SAM
members.note: hypernetwork MLP as highest-leverage module

members.one_line: Domain gap localizes to 2-3 'fracture layers' findable by representation-similarity analysis, and LoRA on only those layers matches full-network LoRA
members.note: representation-similarity fracture layers

members.one_line: Attention-LoRA moves 'where', FFN-LoRA moves 'what': a functional dissociation in SAM adaptation exploitable as a diagnostic-driven placement rule
members.note: attention-LoRA moves where, FFN-LoRA moves what

members.one_line: Bias-only tuning of SAM's neck convolutions is the highest-leverage parameters-per-point site in the whole model
members.note: neck-convolution bias-only tuning

members.one_line: A per-block leave-one-in LoRA atlas for SAM: most adaptation gain concentrates in 2 specific blocks, publishable as a reusable placement map
members.note: leave-one-in per-block LoRA atlas

members.one_line: Patch-embedding LoRA is disproportionately effective for sensor-statistics shifts: the cheapest layer nobody adapts because NLP-derived conventions skip it
members.note: patch-embedding LoRA for sensor shifts

members.one_line: The few global-attention blocks are SAM's domain bottleneck: LoRA restricted to them matches all-blocks LoRA, because windowed blocks compute domain-generic local geometry
members.note: global-attention blocks as the domain bottleneck

label: peft_training_mechanics
shared_hypothesis: Optimization mechanics of PEFT on promptable segmentation; distinct mechanisms.

members.one_line: Required LoRA rank scales with prompt ambiguity of the task, not dataset size: a scaling study that would rewrite rank-selection practice
members.note: rank requirement scales with prompt ambiguity, not data size

members.one_line: Zero-initialized LoRA B-matrices make the first epochs decoder-dominated, causing decoder overfitting before the encoder ever adapts — fixable with layerwise warmup scheduling
members.note: zero-init B-matrix decoder-first dynamics; layerwise warmup

members.one_line: LoRA dropout, inherited from NLP recipes, is systematically harmful for prompt-conditioned segmentation
members.note: LoRA dropout systematically harmful here

members.one_line: Trained LoRAs on SAM collapse to effective rank 1-2 regardless of nominal rank — rank-1 with tuned scale may match rank-16 everywhere
members.note: trained LoRAs collapse to effective rank 1-2

members.one_line: LayerNorm-affine-only tuning acts as 'domain whitening' and wins specifically where the shift is global (contrast inversion, intensity remapping) with tiny labeled sets
members.note: LayerNorm-affine tuning as domain whitening for global shifts

members.one_line: Box-prompt and point-prompt supervision pull SAM's encoder in measurably conflicting directions during PEFT — prompt-type-conditioned adapters remove the conflict
members.note: box-vs-point supervision gradient conflict; prompt-conditioned adapters

members.one_line: Homogeneous-prompt batches train faster: mixing prompt types within a batch creates gradient interference that per-batch grouping removes at zero cost
members.note: homogeneous-prompt batches remove gradient interference

label: forgetting_mitigation
shared_hypothesis: Forecasting and mitigating zero-shot forgetting; distinct methods (diagnosis in XD-09).

members.one_line: Adapter norm growth during training forecasts zero-shot forgetting before any held-out evaluation: an early-stopping signal requiring no generic validation data
members.note: adapter norm growth forecasts forgetting; early stopping

members.one_line: Weight decay on LoRA parameters is a continuous forgetting knob: because decay pulls toward the zero-update (pretrained) function, one scalar trades in-domain gain against zero-shot retention smoothly
members.note: weight decay as continuous forgetting knob

members.one_line: Anchor-prompt rehearsal: storing ~100 (image-embedding, prompt, mask) triplets and replaying them in embedding space prevents forgetting at near-zero cost — no images retained
members.note: anchor-prompt embedding-space rehearsal

label: adapter_algebra_weightspace
shared_hypothesis: Weight-space structure and algebra of adapters; distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: Task arithmetic on mask-token embeddings: tuned token deltas for different shifts (thin-structure, low-contrast) compose additively
members.note: task arithmetic on mask-token deltas composes additively

members.one_line: Orthogonality regularization between domain adapters enables interference-free multi-domain serving on one frozen SAM
members.note: orthogonality regularization for interference-free multi-domain

members.one_line: Merging sequential-task adapters by concatenate-then-SVD-truncate retains both tasks better than weight averaging: a testable claim about the geometry of segmentation adapters
members.note: concatenate-then-SVD-truncate beats weight averaging

members.one_line: Router-free adapter zoos: selecting the right domain adapter by nearest-centroid on pooled SAM embeddings works >95% of the time — serving infrastructure nobody needs to train
members.note: router-free nearest-centroid adapter selection

members.one_line: A computable merge-compatibility score: Fisher-information overlap between adapters predicts whether merging them will hurt, before you merge
members.note: Fisher-overlap merge-compatibility score

members.one_line: Constructive interference exists: adapting to domain B sometimes improves already-deployed domain A, and the direction is predictable from label-style similarity, not image similarity
members.note: constructive interference predictable from label-style similarity

members.one_line: Adapters cluster by imaging physics in weight space: hierarchical clustering of independently trained LoRAs recovers the sensor taxonomy, enabling nearest-physics initialization that halves label needs
members.note: adapters cluster by imaging physics; nearest-physics init

members.one_line: Full fine-tuning deltas are low-rank in SAM's encoder but full-rank in its decoder: measure where low-rank assumptions actually hold, explaining mixed LoRA-on-decoder results
members.note: full-FT deltas low-rank in encoder, full-rank in decoder

members.one_line: SAM's decoder is backbone-agnostic: transplant the frozen prompt-encoder+decoder onto a different frozen encoder (e.g., a self-supervised ViT) with only a trained linear bridge — promptability as a portable interface
members.note: decoder transplant onto different frozen encoder via linear bridge

label: test_time_adaptation_methods
shared_hypothesis: Label-free test-time adaptation mechanisms; distinct losses/criteria (safety inversion in DG-19).

members.one_line: Single-image TTA for SAM: enforce mask consistency across jittered prompts, updating only LayerNorm affines — adaptation from one unlabeled test image
members.note: single-image jitter-consistency TTA on LayerNorm affines

members.one_line: Cyclic prompt-mask self-supervision: derive prompts from SAM's own output mask, re-predict, and demand a fixed point — a label-free adaptation loss with a built-in sanity semantics
members.note: cyclic prompt-mask fixed-point self-supervision

members.one_line: Multimask-entropy as a TTA stopping criterion: stop adapting when hypothesis diversity stops shrinking — a label-free convergence detector
members.note: multimask-entropy stopping criterion

members.one_line: Training-free adaptation by memory: retrieve nearest SA-1B-like embedding neighborhoods and interpolate their decoder behavior for the current image
members.note: training-free retrieval-based decoder-behavior interpolation

members.one_line: In-context segmentation through embedding correspondence: use a reference image+mask as a 'visual prompt' via frozen-feature matching, and measure the true capacity limits of training-free one-shot transfer
members.note: in-context segmentation via frozen-feature correspondence; capacity limits

label: novel_adapter_mechanisms
shared_hypothesis: New adapter families beyond LoRA; distinct mechanisms.

members.one_line: Attention-bias PEFT: adapt SAM by learning additive attention-logit biases (relative-position deltas) instead of weight deltas — geometry-targeted adaptation at ~0.001% parameters
members.note: attention-logit bias PEFT; geometry-targeted

members.one_line: Background-token pruning during adaptation is a regularizer: dropping low-relevance tokens from global attention improves OOD boundary precision by removing background interference
members.note: background-token pruning as regularizer (tension with XD-11)

members.one_line: A tiny frequency-domain adapter branch (FFT features injected at the neck) rescues domains where SAM's spatial features are blind, e.g., low-contrast periodic textures
members.note: FFT sidecar branch at the neck

members.one_line: The 'optical adapter': a single tuned 3x3 input convolution (dozens of parameters) matches encoder LoRA on intensity-remapped domains — the domain gap is at the sensor, fix it at the sensor
members.note: single tuned input conv: fix sensor shifts at the sensor

members.one_line: Linear adapters provably cannot express contrast inversion: a class of domain shifts where LoRA must fail and tiny gated (nonlinear) adapters must win
members.note: linear adapters provably cannot express contrast inversion

members.one_line: A scanline state-space sidecar gives frozen SAM long-range thin-structure continuity: connectivity metrics improve with zero change to region IoU, targeting the exact failure everyone reports
members.note: scanline state-space sidecar for thin-structure continuity

members.one_line: Zero-init channel grafting: add extra sensor channels (depth, NIR, phase) to frozen SAM via a zero-initialized projection that provably preserves zero-shot behavior at step 0, dominating dual-encoder fusion in small-data regimes
members.note: zero-init channel grafting preserving zero-shot at step 0

members.one_line: The 256-channel neck bottleneck measurably discards domain-relevant information: a parallel 32-channel bypass recovers it, quantifying how much adaptation headroom the architecture itself caps
members.note: parallel 32-channel neck bypass quantifies architecture cap

label: data_supervision_protocols
shared_hypothesis: Training-data and prompt-supervision protocol effects; distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: Prompt curriculum determines what adapters learn: easy-to-ambiguous prompt ordering steers PEFT toward boundary skill vs semantic skill — training-data order as an uncontrolled variable in every SAM paper
members.note: prompt curriculum steers boundary-vs-semantic skill

members.one_line: Scribble-only adaptation via self-label completion: use frozen SAM's own prompt mechanism to densify sparse scribbles into training masks, and characterize when the confirmation-bias loop helps vs poisons
members.note: scribble self-label completion; confirmation-bias regimes

members.one_line: Prompt dropout during PEFT: randomly hiding clicks at training time buys robustness to under-specified prompts at deployment — a deliberate, quantified trade against fully-specified accuracy
members.note: prompt dropout for under-specified deployment prompts

label: meta_science_audits
shared_hypothesis: Meta-scientific audits of the adaptation literature; distinct confounds (see also XD-16).

members.one_line: Contradictory 'LoRA works/doesn't work on SAM' findings trace to the alpha/rank scale factor: a meta-scientific audit with a corrective recipe
members.note: alpha/rank scale factor explains contradictory LoRA findings

members.one_line: The popular batch-norm test-time-adaptation family silently no-ops on SAM (LayerNorm has no batch statistics) — an audit of TTA methods that vision practitioners port without checking
members.note: batch-norm TTA silently no-ops on LayerNorm models

members.one_line: Two adapters with equal mIoU can differ 2x in prompt-sensitivity variance: report variance-over-prompts as a first-class metric or ship lotteries
members.note: variance-over-prompts as first-class reported metric

members.one_line: A domain-gap decomposition protocol: swap oracle components (embeddings, prompts, decoder) between in-domain and OOD pipelines to attribute the gap — the missing diagnostic standard for adaptation papers
members.note: oracle component-swap domain-gap decomposition protocol

label: failure_probes_safety
shared_hypothesis: Distinct failure probes and security analyses.

members.one_line: Does SAM think shadows belong to objects? A systematic attached-shadow inclusion bias exists and can be toggled by steering a single direction in prompt-embedding space
members.note: attached-shadow inclusion bias steerable by one direction

members.one_line: Prompt teleportation in periodic textures: clicks on one instance of a repeating pattern select a different instance, revealing position-appearance binding failure in the decoder
members.note: prompt teleportation in periodic textures

members.one_line: Adapter backdoors: a poisoned LoRA can hide trigger-conditioned mask manipulation that is invisible on clean benchmarks — demonstrate feasibility and a spectral detection defense
members.note: adapter backdoors and spectral detection defense

label: efficiency_serving
shared_hypothesis: Efficiency and serving structure; distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: The embedding-cache shortcut defines a measurable 'decoder-only ceiling': map which task families PEFT can solve with 1000x cheaper cached-embedding training
members.note: decoder-only ceiling map with cached embeddings

members.one_line: Refinement clicks don't need the full encoder: cached mid-layer features suffice for click updates, enabling early-exit interactive SAM
members.note: early-exit interactive refinement on cached mid-layer features

label: representation_audits
shared_hypothesis: Frozen-representation property audits; distinct invariances.

members.one_line: SAM is strongly shape-biased (trained on masks, not labels), so style/texture augmentation during PEFT is mostly wasted compute — a testable claim against inherited fine-tuning folklore
members.note: shape bias makes texture augmentation wasted compute

members.one_line: SAM's decisions ride the phase spectrum: amplitude-spectrum swaps barely change its masks, enabling amplitude-only augmentation as a near-free domain randomizer
members.note: phase-spectrum reliance; amplitude-only randomization

members.one_line: A single linear 'mask affordance' direction in SAM's feature space predicts whether an object is segmentable at all — triage before you adapt
members.note: linear mask-affordance direction predicts segmentability

label: medical_signal_physics
shared_hypothesis: Medical acquisition-physics effects on foundation models; distinct mechanisms per physics factor.

members.one_line: Foundation models systematically truncate structures at partial-volume ends, and the truncation length is predictable from the point spread function.
members.note: partial-volume truncation predictable from PSF

members.one_line: On core-versus-whole lesion tasks, foundation models select a fixed operating point on the local intensity distribution rather than understanding the task distinction.
members.note: core-vs-whole tasks solved as fixed intensity operating point

members.one_line: Per-image intensity normalization in foundation-model pipelines discards absolute CT calibration, measurably hurting tasks that depend on Hounsfield semantics.
members.note: per-image normalization discards Hounsfield semantics; near w14_p1b_014 (XD-16 preprocessing dominance)

members.one_line: Foundation models cannot identify MR sequence type from image content alone, and their segmentation errors trace to sequence confusion.
members.note: MR sequence-type confusion drives errors

members.one_line: Ultrasound speckle is discriminative signal that foundation-model invariances destroy: speckle-preserving pipelines will beat speckle-suppressing ones on tissue-differentiation tasks.
members.note: speckle is signal; invariances destroy it

members.one_line: Foundation-model feature quality degrades non-linearly with slice thickness, with a breakpoint set by pretraining resolution statistics rather than anatomy.
members.note: slice-thickness breakpoint set by pretraining statistics; near w14_p1b_034 (anisotropic PSF baked in)

members.one_line: MR undersampling artifacts create structured segmentation failures that image-domain fine-tuning cannot remove, because aliasing is non-local.
members.note: non-local aliasing unfixable by image-domain fine-tuning

members.one_line: Foundation models conflate contrast-agent phases, and phase-swapped test cases reveal that vessel and lesion segmentation rely on phase-specific shortcuts.
members.note: contrast-phase conflation shortcuts

label: volumetric_3d_structure
shared_hypothesis: 2D-vs-3D dimensionality effects; distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: Through-plane topological defects of slice-wise foundation models scale predictably with inter-slice anatomy decorrelation, giving a computable reliability map.
members.note: through-plane defects scale with inter-slice decorrelation

members.one_line: Multi-slice context helps only until the anatomical correlation length is covered, after which added slices contribute nothing, a measurable saturation law.
members.note: context saturates at anatomical correlation length

members.one_line: Isotropic resampling before inference hurts foundation models on native anisotropic data, contrary to standard practice, because it destroys in-plane detail the models rely on.
members.note: isotropic resampling hurts on native anisotropic data

members.one_line: Foundation models ignore contralateral symmetry: occluding one body side leaves predictions on the other side unchanged, unlike human readers.
members.note: contralateral symmetry unused; occlusion test

members.one_line: Slice-shuffle invariance quantifies how much volumetric order information current pipelines actually use, and the answer is close to none for 2D-plus-stitching systems.
members.note: slice-shuffle invariance quantifies unused order information

members.one_line: Tubular-tree breaks in stitched 2D foundation-model outputs follow a characteristic break-length distribution predictable from slice spacing and vessel angle.
members.note: tubular break-length distribution from slice spacing; near w14_p1b_025 (same through-plane defect mechanism, tubular arm)

members.one_line: Errors on thin structures are direction-dependent, aligned with the acquisition axis, and are not removed by isotropic resampling, revealing that the anisotropic PSF is baked into learned features.
members.note: direction-dependent thin-structure errors; anisotropic PSF baked into features; near w14_p1b_018

members.one_line: At matched compute, 3D-native pretraining on modest medical data beats 2D foundation-model transfer only for structures with high through-plane curvature, a testable dichotomy that rationalizes the conflicting literature.
members.note: 3D-native wins only at high through-plane curvature; dichotomy

members.one_line: Registration-free label propagation via foundation-model correspondence beats classical deformable registration only above a deformation-magnitude threshold, giving a measurable regime map for when learned correspondence pays.
members.note: learned correspondence beats registration only above deformation threshold

label: shortcut_structure
shared_hypothesis: Structure of shortcut reliance under distribution shift; distinct hypotheses (position priors in XD-18, fingerprints in XD-51).

members.one_line: Foundation-model features encode acquisition site so strongly that site is linearly decodable better than anatomy, and site-feature removal changes which cases fail, not just averages.
members.note: site decodable better than anatomy; removal changes which cases fail

members.one_line: Lesion-segmentation false-positive rates of foundation models scale with training-set lesion prevalence, making screening-population deployment quantifiably miscalibrated at the population level.
members.note: false-positive rate scales with training lesion prevalence

members.one_line: Medical shortcut features form a stable exploitation hierarchy: models rely on them in a consistent order, and knocking out one shortcut shifts reliance to the next, not to anatomy.
members.note: stable shortcut-exploitation hierarchy; knockout shifts reliance

members.one_line: After image harmonization, the residual cross-site gap concentrates in a small set of structure types, showing harmonization fixes appearance shift but not representation-fragility shift.
members.note: harmonization fixes appearance shift, not representation fragility

label: clinical_reliability_safety
shared_hypothesis: Clinical reliability, stability, and communication; distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: Test-time adaptation improves average Dice while increasing undetected catastrophic failures, a safety inversion measurable as tail-risk versus mean trade-off.
members.note: TTA improves mean while raising undetected catastrophic tail

members.one_line: Voxel-level selective prediction fails clinically because errors are spatially clustered: rejecting the most-uncertain voxels removes scattered noise while leaving coherent wrong regions intact.
members.note: voxel-level selective prediction fails on spatially clustered errors

members.one_line: Model-version updates change segmentations on unchanged patients more than rescan test-retest variation, making churn, not accuracy, the binding constraint for longitudinal clinical use.
members.note: model-version churn exceeds rescan test-retest variation

members.one_line: Communicating segmentation uncertainty as discrete contour bands changes downstream quantitative decisions more than heatmaps do, because band geometry maps directly onto margin decisions.
members.note: contour bands change decisions more than heatmaps

members.one_line: Feature keypoints of foundation models drift under rescanning more than anatomical landmarks do, revealing that learned correspondences are appearance-locked rather than anatomy-locked.
members.note: feature keypoints drift under rescan; appearance-locked correspondence

label: privacy_leakage
shared_hypothesis: Privacy failures of features, adapters, and synthetic data; distinct channels.

members.one_line: Foundation-model embeddings re-identify patients across scans and modalities at rates constituting a quantifiable privacy failure of feature-sharing pipelines.
members.note: embeddings re-identify patients across scans/modalities

members.one_line: Training segmentation models on generatively synthesized medical images reintroduces memorized real-patient content, laundering privacy leakage through the synthetic label.
members.note: synthetic training data launders memorized patient content

members.one_line: Adapter weights from federated medical fine-tuning are invertible enough to reconstruct site-identifying data statistics, undermining the privacy rationale for sharing adapters instead of data.
members.note: federated adapter weights invertible to site statistics

label: language_grounding_medical
shared_hypothesis: Language-grounding failure axes beyond embedding collisions (XD-21) and negation (XD-20); distinct hypotheses.

members.one_line: Report-derived weak supervision for segmentation plateaus at coarse localization: adding more report-image pairs improves detection but not boundary fidelity, an information-theoretic ceiling.
members.note: report-derived supervision plateaus at coarse localization

members.one_line: Medical referring segmentation fails on relational descriptions (posterior to X, between Y and Z) while succeeding on attributive ones, localizing the grounding failure to spatial-relation composition.
members.note: relational (not attributive) grounding is the failing composition

members.one_line: Left-right confusion in text-guided medical segmentation is systematically induced by mirror-symmetric augmentation heritage, and its rate is predictable from augmentation policy of the visual backbone.
members.note: left-right confusion induced by mirror-augmentation heritage

members.one_line: Cross-lingual degradation of medical text-guided segmentation is larger for dense grounding than for image-level tasks, revealing that spatial binding is the most language-fragile layer of multimodal transfer.
members.note: cross-lingual degradation largest for dense grounding

members.one_line: Hedging language in radiology reports (possible, cannot exclude) spatially predicts model-annotator disagreement regions, making report uncertainty a free supervision signal for segmentation reliability.
members.note: report hedging language spatially predicts disagreement; free supervision

label: prompt_ontology_probe
shared_hypothesis: Interpretability probe of what a promptable model treats as an object.

members.one_line: The spatial distribution of effective prompts reveals what a foundation model considers an object in medical images, providing an interpretability tool for its medical ontology.
members.note: spatial distribution of effective prompts reveals the model's medical ontology

label: cheap_physics_features
shared_hypothesis: Handcrafted physics features rivaling deep models on amorphous targets; distinct features/tasks.

members.one_line: A linear probe on local power-spectrum slope beats a linear probe on deep VFM features for smoke detection, showing the backbone discards the best cue.
members.note: power-spectrum slope probe beats deep features for smoke

members.one_line: A two-layer MLP on raw chromaticity rivals fine-tuned foundation models for daytime flame pixels at a thousandth of the compute.
members.note: chromaticity MLP rivals foundation models for daytime flame

members.one_line: A frozen pretrained dehazing network's transmission map, inverted and thresholded, is a zero-training smoke segmenter competitive with trained baselines.
members.note: frozen dehazing transmission map as zero-training segmenter; near w14p1c-096 (same single-scattering physics cue, DG-24)

members.one_line: The true fog-vs-smoke discriminator is the spatial gradient of density, and a handcrafted density-gradient feature beats CLIP embeddings at this distinction.
members.note: density-gradient feature is the true fog-vs-smoke discriminator

label: physics_priors_crossmodal
shared_hypothesis: Physics priors and cross-modal cues; distinct physical mechanisms.

members.one_line: Adding monocular depth as an input channel actively hurts transparent-object segmentation: a clean negative-transfer case.
members.note: monocular depth input hurts transparent objects; TENSION with w14p1c-102 (depth helps robustness)

members.one_line: An RGB-to-polarization-cue predictor, trained once on a small polarized dataset, transfers as a frozen adapter that improves transparent segmentation everywhere.
members.note: RGB-to-polarization-cue predictor as frozen transferable adapter

members.one_line: Smoke density estimates from cross-lens parallax on dual-camera phones give free weak supervision for opacity.
members.note: dual-camera parallax as free opacity supervision

members.one_line: A gravity-aware positional encoding helps smoke segmentation on average but hurts on downdrafts and inversions, and the trade is quantifiable.
members.note: gravity-aware positional encoding helps on average, hurts downdrafts

members.one_line: An advection-consistency loss (masks should warp along smoke flow plus grow at sources) improves temporal stability without any extra labels.
members.note: advection-consistency loss for temporal stability

members.one_line: A per-pixel single-scattering color test (smoke color must be a convex mix of ambient light and transmitted background) reranks SAM proposals into much better smoke masks.
members.note: single-scattering convex-color test reranks SAM proposals

members.one_line: An 8x8-pixel thermopile array fused with an RGB fire segmenter eliminates most reflection and sunset false positives at trivial hardware cost.
